version.changelog:
- Added a prominent privacy warning emphasizing that PDFs, passwords, and signing materials are sent to the configured Stirling-PDF instance.
- Advised users to only set `STIRLING_BASE_URL` to a local or trusted private server, not a public instance.
- No changes to functionality or configuration steps; documentation update only.

llm.summary: This PDF skill mostly matches a self-hosted Stirling-PDF helper, but it includes unsafe helper scripts that can send sensitive PDFs and API keys to an undocumented network address and expose users to command injection.

dimensions.detail: Uploading PDFs and document passwords to a configured API is proportionate for a Stirling-PDF wrapper when clearly controlled, but plaintext HTTP, a fixed undocumented endpoint, positional passwords, and no endpoint validation are not proportionate for sensitive PDF handling.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The Docker deployment instructions are understandable for Stirling-PDF but use frooodle/s-pdf:latest and --restart unless-stopped, which creates mutable dependency and persistent-service risk.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The operational scope is under-specified: the documentation says STIRLING_BASE_URL defaults to localhost, while one shipped helper uses STIRLING_API_URL with a fixed 192.168.31.158 default; merge handling in both scripts also mishandles untrusted filenames.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The skill does not install a local backdoor or modify agent memory, but the documented Docker container is persistent across restarts and stores data/logs under /opt/stirling-pdf.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose is local/private PDF processing through Stirling-PDF, and SKILL.md discloses API uploads to a user-controlled instance, but artifact/scripts/stirling-pdf.sh defaults to an undocumented fixed HTTP LAN endpoint and ignores the documented STIRLING_BASE_URL variable.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Review carefully before installing. Only use this with a Stirling-PDF instance you control, prefer HTTPS for any non-local endpoint, avoid sensitive PDFs until the fixed 192.168.31.158 default and STIRLING_BASE_URL mismatch are removed, and do not use the merge helpers with untrusted filenames. Pin the Docker image to a reviewed digest and avoid passing document passwords as command-line arguments.
llm.findings:
[TP4] expected: Partially accepted: the skill is an API wrapper rather than a full local implementation, but SKILL.md does disclose Stirling-PDF API use; the issue is overstatement and inconsistent helper coverage, not tool poisoning by itself.
[LP3] unexpected: Accepted as a scoping concern: shell and Docker commands are involved, but the skill does not define tight runtime boundaries or safe invocation constraints.
[RP1] unexpected: Accepted as a supply-chain concern: SKILL.md uses a mutable latest Docker image tag for a persistent service.
[SDI-2] unexpected: Accepted for artifact/scripts/stirling-pdf.sh: it uses STIRLING_API_URL and defaults to http://192.168.31.158:3998, which conflicts with the documented STIRLING_BASE_URL localhost behavior.
[SQP-2] unexpected: Accepted in part: uploading PDFs to a Stirling-PDF API is expected, but transmitting PDFs, passwords, and API keys over plaintext HTTP without endpoint validation or runtime warning is a real concern.
[SDI-1] unexpected: Accepted for the fixed-endpoint helper: the privacy model is inconsistent because one script can transmit documents to an undocumented host rather than the user's documented instance.
[SDI-4] expected: Downgraded: artifact/scripts/pdf-toolkit.sh uses the documented STIRLING_BASE_URL defaulting to localhost, and SKILL.md includes an API-upload privacy note, though the local-only language remains overstated.
[SQP-3] expected: Downgraded: the chi_sim+eng OCR default is documented in SKILL.md notes and help text and is not a security-significant issue by itself.
[other] unexpected: Accepted: the static scan's fixed-host concern is supported by artifact/scripts/stirling-pdf.sh lines 6-7 and the mismatch with SKILL.md environment instructions.
[T09] unexpected: Accepted: artifact/scripts/stirling-pdf.sh uses eval for merge command construction, and artifact/scripts/pdf-toolkit.sh expands a constructed curl fragment unquoted, creating command or argument injection risk from filenames or environment values.
[T08] unexpected: Accepted as a non-malicious but meaningful dependency risk because the deployment command pulls an unpinned latest container image.
